title: Thai-Style Red Curry Fish Cakes with Sweet Chili Dip
dek: Fresh white fish, red curry paste and crisp green beans become springy, golden-edged cakes with a bright lime-sweet chili dip and cool lettuce for wrapping.
image_alt: Golden Thai-style fish cakes with green bean and red pepper pieces on curly lettuce beside sweet chili dipping sauce
ingredients: 1 lb skinless boneless white fish fillets, such as pollock, cod or tilapia, thawed if frozen and very cold
3 oz green beans, trimmed and sliced crosswise 1/8 inch thick (about 2/3 cup)
1/3 cup finely diced red bell pepper
1/4 cup neutral high-heat oil, such as avocado or canola, plus more if needed
1 small head green leaf lettuce, leaves separated, washed and thoroughly dried

instructions.name: Dry and chill the fish
instructions.text: Pat the fish very dry, remove any pin bones and cut it into 1-inch pieces. Put the fish and processor blade in the freezer for 10 minutes; the fish should feel firm and cold but must not refreeze solid. This chilling time is included in the total time.

instructions.name: Mix the lime-sweet chili dip
instructions.text: Stir the sweet chili sauce, 1 tablespoon lime juice and rice vinegar in a small serving bowl. Set it aside while the cakes cook. Keep the lettuce leaves dry so they remain crisp enough to hold a hot fish cake.

instructions.name: Process a springy fish paste
instructions.text: Put the chilled fish, egg, red curry paste, fish sauce, brown sugar, lime zest and cornstarch in the cold food processor. Pulse 12 to 15 times, scraping once, until the mixture becomes cohesive and sticky but still shows tiny pieces of fish; do not run the machine continuously or let the paste become warm.

instructions.name: Fold in the visible vegetables
instructions.text: Transfer the fish paste to a bowl and fold in the sliced green beans, diced red pepper and scallions until evenly distributed. With damp hands, divide the mixture into eight 1/3-cup portions and shape each into an oval cake about 3/4 inch thick. Put them on a parchment-lined plate.

instructions.name: Shallow-fry in two batches
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat until shimmering, about 2 minutes; the oil should be near 350°F. Add four cakes without crowding and cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, adjusting the heat so they brown steadily rather than scorch. Transfer to a wire rack and repeat with the remaining oil and cakes.

instructions.name: Verify doneness and dress the lettuce
instructions.text: Check the thickest cake in each batch with a clean instant-read thermometer; the center must reach 145°F and look opaque. Toss the lettuce gently with the remaining 1 tablespoon lime juice and the salt only after the last batch is cooked.

instructions.name: Plate to match the finished dish
instructions.text: Arrange the lettuce on a platter and set the fish cakes on top. Serve two cakes per person with the sweet chili dip on the side, letting diners wrap bites in the crisp leaves.

why_it_works: Very cold fish and short pulses keep the proteins from overheating while building the sticky paste that gives the cakes a resilient, springy center.
Cornstarch absorbs surface moisture and supports the egg, so the cakes hold together without a breadcrumb coating that would hide the fish and vegetables.
Thin green-bean coins and a fine pepper dice soften during the brief fry while remaining clearly visible in the browned cakes shown in the photograph.
Two uncrowded batches keep the oil temperature steadier, producing browned edges before the 3/4-inch centers pass 145°F.
Lime and rice vinegar sharpen bottled sweet chili sauce, balancing the savory fish sauce and rich shallow-fried exterior without pouring a glaze over the cakes.
swaps: Use pollock, cod, tilapia or another lean, boneless white fish in the same weight. Oily fish such as salmon produces a softer, richer cake and may need 1 additional tablespoon cornstarch.
For a milder batch, use 1 tablespoon red curry paste and add 1 tablespoon tomato paste; curry-paste brands vary in heat and salt.
Replace the green beans with finely sliced snap peas. Keep the pieces thin so they become tender within the short skillet time.
For a gluten-free version, verify that the red curry paste, fish sauce, sweet chili sauce and cornstarch are certified gluten-free because formulas vary by brand.
storage: Cool leftover fish cakes within 2 hours and refrigerate them separately from the lettuce and dip in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the cakes on a rack in a 375°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes, or in a 350°F air fryer for 4 to 6 minutes, until the centers reach 165°F. Freeze cooked, cooled cakes between parchment sheets for up to 2 months; thaw overnight before reheating. Do not freeze the lettuce.
notes: Thaw frozen fish overnight in the refrigerator, then press it between clean towels. Excess water prevents the paste from becoming sticky and can make the oil spit.
Red curry paste and fish sauce can contain shellfish or other allergens, and sodium levels vary. Check both labels when cooking for allergies or salt-sensitive diners.
If you do not have a food processor, mince the fish finely with a heavy chef's knife, then stir it vigorously with the egg, seasonings and cornstarch for 2 minutes until tacky.
Do not press the cakes after they enter the skillet. Their measured thickness and an instant-read thermometer give a more reliable doneness check than firmness or color alone.
Calories and cost include two fish cakes, one quarter of the dipping sauce and lettuce per serving; actual values vary with the fish species, oil absorption and local prices.

faqs.q: Why did my Thai-style fish cakes fall apart?
faqs.a: The fish was probably too wet, too warm or insufficiently processed. Pat it dry, chill it before pulsing and continue only until the paste looks sticky. Shape with damp hands, then wait for a firm brown crust before turning each cake once.

faqs.q: Can I shape the fish cakes ahead of dinner?
faqs.a: Yes. Shape them up to 8 hours ahead, cover the plate tightly and refrigerate it at 40°F or below. Keep the raw cakes cold until the skillet is ready, and cook every cake to 145°F. Mix the dip up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate it separately.

faqs.q: Can I bake these red curry fish cakes instead of frying them?
faqs.a: Yes, although the surface will be less craggy than the photographed shallow-fried version. Brush both sides with oil and bake on a parchment-lined sheet at 425°F for 8 minutes, flip, then bake 6 to 8 minutes more until browned and 145°F in the center.
